system_description.narrative_title: Wave of political upheaval and market shocks
system_description.narrative_summary: A synchronized surge of mass protests and surprise electoral upsets — from violent demonstrations in France to Lula’s comeback in Brazil and Serbia’s student victory — is producing acute political volatility and triggering market reactions. The phenomenon functions as an open system: grievances, mobilization, electoral shocks, policy responses and investor flows circulate across borders and media, producing reinforcing and balancing feedbacks (protests → political moves → market/foreign reactions → further protests or concessions). Short-term catalysts (elections, violent incidents) and persistent structural pressures (cost of living, corruption, weakening trust in institutions) feed the system and transmit impacts internationally.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary: national mass protests and demonstrations, surprise or contested election results, incumbent and opposition political actors, security and policing responses, market investor reactions (stocks, currency), media and social-media amplification, immediate policy decisions and legal contests.
system_description.super_system: Global political-economic order (international markets, geopolitical alignments, transnational information flows and democratic norms).

variables.name: Public grievance intensity
variables.description: Aggregate level of population-perceived economic and political grievances driving discontent.

variables.name: Protest mobilization rate
variables.description: Speed at which individuals are recruited or mobilized into collective demonstrations and actions.

variables.name: Protest magnitude
variables.description: Current aggregated scale of public demonstrations measured by participants, events and geographic spread.

variables.name: Protest violence level
variables.description: Prevalence and severity of violent tactics and clashes occurring within protest events.

variables.name: Election surprise potential
variables.description: Systemic probability and magnitude of unexpected or contested electoral outcomes altering political balance.

variables.name: Incumbent legitimacy
variables.description: Public and elite perception of the political authority and mandate of current officeholders.

variables.name: Security response intensity
variables.description: Scale and aggressiveness of policing, security and coercive measures deployed in response to unrest.

variables.name: Policy concession rate
variables.description: Speed and magnitude at which authorities implement concessions, reforms or relief measures in response to pressures.

variables.name: Legal contestation activity
variables.description: Intensity of judicial, administrative and procedural challenges used to dispute political or electoral outcomes.

variables.name: Investor capital flow
variables.description: Net pace and direction of portfolio and capital movements into or out of the domestic market in response to political signals.

variables.name: Asset price volatility
variables.description: Degree of short-term variability in key asset prices and exchange rates reflecting market instability.

variables.name: Investor risk sentiment
variables.description: Aggregate market perception of political and economic risk influencing risk appetite and portfolio decisions.

variables.name: Media amplification strength
variables.description: Rate and intensity with which traditional media frames and spreads information about protests and political events.

variables.name: Social-media virality
variables.description: Speed and reach of protest-related content propagation across social platforms and networks.

variables.name: Cross-border signal transmission
variables.description: Strength and speed of political, informational and financial shock propagation across national boundaries.

variables.name: Institutional trust level
variables.description: Aggregate public confidence in core institutions such as government, judiciary and electoral systems.

catalysts.title: Continued mass protests in France
catalysts.description: Ongoing nationwide demonstrations and student vows to keep protesting are likely to sustain large-scale unrest and political pressure on the Macron government.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Hundreds of Thousands Protest Across France'; 'French students vow more protests despite Macron concessions'.

catalysts.title: Post-election legal and political challenge in Brazil
catalysts.description: Bolsonaro's refusal to concede and announced plans to seek annulment, plus external endorsements, are likely to trigger legal fights and street mobilization.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Bolsonaro refuses to concede, says he will seek annulment'; 'Trump says Brazil election looked "rigged"'.

catalysts.title: Sustained market turmoil in Brazil
catalysts.description: Investor reactions to Lula's surprise win are likely to sustain capital outflows, currency weakness and elevated asset volatility in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Brazil stocks, real tumble'; 'Brazilian Markets Crash After Lula’s Surprise Election Win'.

catalysts.title: Israeli national election (voter return wave)
catalysts.description: Imminent national voting—with tens of thousands flying back to vote—can produce surprise outcomes, mobilize supporters and shape short-term political legitimacy.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Israeli election draws tens of thousands of citizens flying back to vote'; 'What’s on the Line as Israelis Prepare to Vote'.

catalysts.title: Escalation and international fallout around Israel–Gaza/West Bank
catalysts.description: UN findings and calls for lockdowns, plus ongoing operations, raise odds of further violence, international legal pressure and diaspora protests.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide'; 'Netanyahu Calls for West Bank Lockdown After Deadly Attack'.

catalysts.title: Transition to student-backed government in Serbia
catalysts.description: Historic student election victory creates a transition period with governance risks and uncertain effects on institutional trust and regional alignment.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Serbia’s ex-president Vučić concedes defeat'; 'After Vucic defeat, Serbia waits to see how student-backed leaders will govern'.

catalysts.title: Return of opposition leader María Corina Machado
catalysts.description: Machado's return from exile is likely to boost opposition organizing and protests, testing the regime and international responses.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Venezuela opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returns to Venezuela'; 'What María Corina Machado’s Return Means for Venezuela'.

catalysts.title: Aftermath of Lisbon housing protest camp clearance
catalysts.description: Police clearing of a high-profile housing camp could spur renewed demonstrations and wider housing movement activism across Portugal and Europe.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Portuguese police clear Lisbon housing protest camp, make arrests' (Oct 25/26).
